newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DBS to buy 60 pct of Sri Dhana Finance.
newsitem.headline: DBS to buy 60 pct of Sri Dhana Finance.

text.p: The Development Bank of Singapore Ltd (DBS) said on Monday it had agreed to buy a controlling 60 percent stake in Thailand's Sri Dhana Finance Public Co Ltd.
DBS said in a statement it currently owns 9.5 percent of Sri Dhana.
It said it had signed a memorandum of understanding with the Thai company which agreed the acquisition was subject to a number of conditions. These included:
- approval for the acquisition by the Ministry of Finance of Thailand and other relevant authorities
- a waiver from regulatory authorities from the normal requirement to make a mandatory takeover offer for the rest of the company's shares

- additional licences to operate fixed and savings deposit account business, foreign exchange and letters of credit business, and permission to establish new branches in Bangkok and other areas, or a commercial banking licence
- and continued funding assistance by Bank of Thailand.

The DBS statement quoted DBS president and chief operating officer Ng Kee Choe as saying there were many conditions to be fulfilled before a deal was struck and the process was likely to take a few months.
